title: Resolve defined-term cross-references in a merger agreement
instructions: For each queried term: return (1) the definition verbatim with its section, (2) every section where the term creates or modifies an obligation, quoted briefly, and (3) any related defined terms the definition itself depends on. Precision matters more than recall — returning the wrong passage is worse than returning fewer, exact ones.

inputs.name: merger-agreement-corpus/
inputs.description: Long-form agreements with dense cross-references and defined-term chains.

inputs.name: queries.json
inputs.description: Terms to resolve, one per query.

sample_answer:
DEFINED-TERM RESOLUTION

Term: Company Material Adverse Effect
Definition (verbatim, s. 3.1(f)): 'any event, change, circumstance or effect that, individually or in the aggregate with all other such events, has had or would reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on the business, assets, or financial condition of the Company and its Subsidiaries, taken as a whole.'
Related terms: 'Subsidiaries' (s. 3.1(g)); see the materiality definitions annex.
Operative uses: s. 6.2(a) (closing condition — no CMAE since signing); s. 9.1(b) (termination right if CMAE persists 90 days).

Term: Working Capital
Definition (verbatim, s. 2.3(h)) — retrieved: 'the current assets minus current liabilities of the Company, determined in accordance with GAAP as in effect at signing.'
Operative uses: s. 2.3 (purchase price adjustment against the peg).

rubric.criterion: Returns the verbatim definition with the correct section for each query
Identifies the sections where the term drives an obligation
Follows defined-term chains the definition depends on
Returns a passage that is not the definition or an operative use (penalty)

not_contains_any: the recitals mention the founders' vision

rubric.criterion: Every returned passage carries its section reference
Verbatim quotes match the corpus exactly
